author: Yffe
content: Root cause: `as` binds tighter than the binary/unary operators in both Verus and Rust, but every cast-emit site in the lowering used a bare format!("{inner} as {ty}") / format!("{lowered} as usize"). A cast over a binary inner thus mis-binds: (n-1) as nat -> n - 1 as nat = n - (1 as nat) (int/nat mismatch, L0); (i-1) as usize -> i - (1 as usize) (u64-usize, E0277). Fix the CAUSE for the whole class: parenthesize the inner ONLY when it is an Expr::Binary/Unary (a simple inner never mis-binds, so corpus/golden simple casts stay byte-identical — no regression). Sites fixed in lower.rs + l1.rs: the Expr::Cast arm, the byte_at/slice 'as usize' coercion, the split 'as u8' coercion, and lower_index_arg's combinator 'as int'. Authority: tests/golden/lower/parse_u64.verus.rs (hand-authored) already writes the paren'd form '(k - 1) as nat' / '(s.len() - 1) as int'.
